assessment.mechanisms: Two mechanisms account for the accepted findings. Each correction narrowed the end rule by one case and the next round found the case beside it; the round 3 correction bounds it structurally instead (the declaration stop applies only after a type has ended, reserved words that cannot start a type end it anywhere), which is the first version of the rule stated as a property rather than a list of cases. (2) Diagnostic and lowering ownership of the new continuation token: round 1 grammar finding 1 (the new unread token bypassed the shared ownership table) and round 3 undirected finding 1 (a member line that continues a type and begins a statement was skipped by the lowerer as type-only text, dropping an assignment with no error), fixed by routing the token through the shared table and lowering such lines as block children. Round 1 ax's finding was the CI consequence of the first mechanism (43 tests in 10 files writing `&` in function bodies), and round 2's second finding was test honesty (two runtime cases passed with the correction reverted), fixed by cases that fail without it.
assessment.regressions: No correction introduced a defect that a later reviewer attributed to it as a regression; each later finding was a neighbouring case the narrowed end rule still missed, or an ownership gap the new token exposed. The test-honesty finding in round 2 shows one verification lapse (runtime cases that did not depend on the grammar change), corrected with cases that fail on revert and restored by SHA-256. The round 3 corrections are each pinned by a test that fails with the change undone.
assessment.repairOptions: The round 3 correction already is the broader repair for mechanism 1: a declaration stop conditioned on a completed type rather than an enumerated list of stop words.
